merge.title: Option-byte posture: pin the unpinned masks on silicon (OEM-lock bits are wrong today), make the surviving production-silent verdicts halt, measure the whole slot window, and keep halt (not wipe) as the mismatch response
merge.threat: Transit or factory attacker on an RDP-0 ship unit who (a) plants an OEM1/OEM2 RDP-regression key, making the later RDP-2 reversible to RDP-1 without erasing code; the key value is write-only and FLASH_NSSR.OEMxLOCK is the only observable. (b) Clears or narrows WRP on the FSBL pages before the self-lock, so RDP-2 freezes a writable trust root and invariant #10 is forfeited for that die. (c) Leaves BOOT_LOCK clear so SECBOOTADD0 and SWAP_BANK stay mutable at RDP-2. (d) Lowers BOR_LEV to ease voltage glitching. (e) Pre-stages a payload in the unmeasured tail of a slot. Secondary: a post-lock boot that bypasses the FSBL (redirected SECBOOTADD0) currently produces no effect in a production image. Not addressed: an RDP glitch at option-byte load, which opens debug before any firmware instruction runs.
merge.proposal:
One work package in five ordered parts. No wipe, no on-device option-byte write other than RDP.

A. Silicon pin ceremony (extends #46, #387, #400, #45, #753; one sacrificial U585CIU6 plus read-back on both boards).
- Correct OEM1LOCK/OEM2LOCK to FLASH_NSSR bits 18/19. shared/src/lockdown.rs:279-280 has 1<<26 / 1<<27, which are reserved bits; the register offset read (FLASH_NS+0x20) is right.
- Positive detection: provision an OEM1 key at RDP-0 and confirm the predicate trips. Then confirm that a factory write of OEMxKEYR = 0xFFFFFFFF clears the lock bit, and check OPTWERR.
- Pin the WRP1AR/WRP2AR layout (STRT, END, UNLOCK), BOOT_LOCK and BOR_LEV[10:8]. Decide an exact OPTR expected value plus don't-care mask (SL9: nSWBOOT0, nBOOT0, NRST_MODE are not compared today).
- Only then flip OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED and WRP1A_MASK_PINNED. Flip require_boot_lock after #753 fixes the factory order (SECBOOTADD0/SWAP_BANK before BOOT_LOCK).
- Promote BOR_LEV from advisory to a hard field.

B. Widen the every-boot check once pinned.
- FSBL tz-1 (fsbl/src/optbytes.rs) moves from verify_confirmed_fields to the full phase profile: WRP1A, WRP2A, OEM locks, BOOT_LOCK, BOR_LEV. It stays read-only, two-pass persistent, halt-only. About +100-200 B, which must land before the #540 geometry freeze.
- Add a secure-world re-check on every RDP-2 boot before SE unlock, since first_boot returns immediately at L2 (first_boot/mod.rs:174-176). Trezor repeats the OEM check in its kernel (kernel/main.c:180-181).
- Response is halt with an E08xx screen.

C. Make the production-silent verdicts executable.
- The SECBOOTADD0 check at secure/src/main.rs:1280-1290 has no action outside secure_log!. Give it a sentinel-gated halt under mode-production.
- Resolve #192: remove or fence rdp-enforce-halt against rdp2-self-lock, and state that Phase A is the pre-ALL_DONE RDP gate.
- Add a source-invariant host test that fails on any security verdict branch in a mode-production cfg whose only effect is secure_log!. It must demonstrably fail on the pre-fix lines.

D. Whole-slot-window measurement.
- FSBL verify_images hashes the declared length, then requires [len, SLOT_*_CAPACITY) to be 0xFF. This is Trezor's check_image_contents padding check, not Krux random fill.
- fw_update COMMIT verifies the tail is erased.
- Leave the measured_boot hash range and the 8 words unchanged; add only the tail-is-0xFF check in the secure world so the two rows stay identical.

E. Cheap adjuncts.
- Pass the already-classified reset cause (main.rs:1186) into Phase A and refuse the RDP burn after Watchdog, LowPower or Unknown. Park and re-prompt, never halt. Allow Cold, and Software on the documented re-prompt path.
- Add FLASH_NSSR bits 18/19, WRP1AR/WRP2AR, the BOOT_LOCK bit and BOR_LEV to the published SWD connect-under-reset checklist (docs/security/user-device-verification.md) and to the #595 factory record.
- The factory, not Phase A, writes OEMxKEYR = 0xFFFFFFFF as its "OEM-key finalization" step.

dropped_parts: Wipe or BHK-erase on option-byte mismatch (IMP-06 item 4, FI-06 item 1, BOOT-01 item 4, BOOT-06 items 1 and 3, FWU-6 item 3). Against recorded decisions: owner decision 2026-07-23 (fw-rollback-draft12-candidate-2026-07-21.md:397-407, tz-1 halts on persistent mismatch and never writes) and trezor-comparison-critical-port-2026-06.md:44,79 (reserve the destructive SE wipe for confirmed TAMP/GTZC tamper; do not infer SE-wipe authority). Also low value: no plaintext seed is on the MCU at that point, and a real RDP regression gives the attacker debug halt before any firmware runs. It is an FI brick lever, and it collides with BHK recoverability (#707/#712). The FSBL variant is additionally a no-op: the FSBL has no flash-write path and the page-125 flag's consumer never runs while the FSBL halts.

Phase A writing OEM1KEYR/OEM2KEYR = 0xFFFFFFFF (IMP-06, FI-06, FWU-6). Violates first-boot-requirements.md R2.1 (must not program any option byte other than RDP) and Draft 1.2 corollary C1 (absolute). first-boot-provisioning.md:46-50 assigns OEM-key finalization to the factory. Re-scoped to a factory step plus the Phase-A read check.

FSBL refusing to branch on OBLRSTF/IWDG/WWDG (IMP-06 item 3). OBLRSTF is set by the legitimate first-boot OBL_LAUNCH. Sticky flags without RMVF make any watchdog bite a permanent no-boot, and clearing them in the FSBL starves secure/src/reset_cause.rs. A glitched option-byte load sets no flag. Trezor's reset_flags_check has zero callers.
Normal-boot POR-only rule as 'Trezor's rule' (BOOT-06 item 2). Trezor does not call it (only reset_flags_reset at boardloader/main.c:323). Reduced to an input to the Phase-A burn decision.

Fatal die-id check (BOOT-06 item 1). die_id.rs:22-30 deliberately scopes it as a report, not a fault: a non-rev-U die is a certificate-scope fact, and an attacker who controls the part can present any IDCODE. No bench die has been through HW-ASSUME-REV-U (#400).
Random-fill-and-pin of slot tails (Krux model, IMP-06 item 2 alternative). Incompatible with the vendor-signed manifest hash and with identical 8 words across units.

Changing the measured_boot::firmware_hash range to the whole window (IMP-06 item 2). measured-boot.md makes the FSBL and secure-world byte-range identity deliberate; a tail-is-0xFF check gives the same guarantee without moving the fingerprint.

BHKLOCK assertion before every sign (FI-06 item 4). No vendor precedent. bhk.rs:390-455 already handles the lock at load and proves the active key by KAT. BHKLOCK is cleared only by tamper or RDP regression, which the retained every-boot option-byte check covers.
HDP1 over the FSBL as a new item (FI-06 item 3). Already #39, #214 and #43; the Trezor precedent hides a secret sector, not reproducible loader code. Pointer only.
The claim that whole-slot hashing adds about 2x FSBL verify time (IMP-06 risks). Round 1 corrected this: the delta is only the tail bytes, as a compare.

merge.untracked_delta:
No issue found for the following (searches: OBLRSTF, slot tail, padding, reset cause, secure_log silent, OEM key, SWD verify NSSR).
1. The OEM1LOCK/OEM2LOCK constants are on reserved bits 26/27; the SVD says 18/19. #46 covers pinning in general but does not record that the current guess is known wrong and would pass vacuously if the flag were flipped.
2. The production-silent SECBOOTADD0 verdict at main.rs:1280-1290, and a source-invariant test against log-only verdicts.
3. Slot-tail 0xFF check in the FSBL, the secure world and fw_update COMMIT.
4. A secure-world every-boot option-byte re-check at RDP-2.
5. Reset cause as an input to the Phase-A burn decision.
6. NSSR OEM lock bits, WRP, BOOT_LOCK and BOR_LEV in the user SWD verification checklist; user-device-verification.md has no OEM/NSSR mention.
7. An exact OPTR compare with a don't-care mask (SL9 is noted in code at lockdown.rs:373-379 as handled separately; no issue located).
8. Promoting BOR_LEV from advisory to a hard field.
decision_conflicts: Wipe on mismatch conflicts with the owner decision of 2026-07-23 (tz-1 halts on persistent mismatch, never writes) and the June-2026 critical-port adjudication (SE wipe reserved for confirmed TAMP/GTZC tamper). Resolved by dropping; re-raising needs new evidence and an owner re-decision.
An on-device OEM key write conflicts with R2.1 and Draft 1.2 C1 (the only on-device option-byte write is the confirm-gated RDP burn). Resolved by moving it to the factory.
Any FSBL flash write conflicts with the FSBL read-only posture (fsbl/src/marker.rs bench-only fence, invariant #10). Resolved: the FSBL stays read-only and halt-only.
Changing the measured-boot hash range conflicts with the deliberate FSBL/secure-world range identity in measured-boot.md. Resolved by a tail check outside the hash.
A fatal die-id conflicts with die_id.rs's stated scope (report, not fault). Resolved by dropping.
Part A consumes sacrificial silicon, and the owner defers irreversible chip work by design. No conflict, but schedule it with the #45/#268 ceremony rather than alone.
New halts must respect #835. The every-boot checks stay two-pass persistent with a visible E08xx code.
hardware_asks: One sacrificial STM32U585CIU6 unit (or bare die on a breakout) for the OEM1-key positive detection and the WRP UNLOCK=0 / BOOT_LOCK dry-run; share it with #45.
Factory line: add 'write OEM1KEYR/OEM2KEYR = 0xFFFFFFFF, then read FLASH_NSSR bits 18/19 = 0' to the option-byte step, and record NSSR, WRP1AR/WRP2AR, SECBOOTADD0R and OPTR per unit (#595).
No board or enclosure change. SWD on SBU for user verification is already requested in user-device-verification.md.
prerequisites: #753 factory sequencing decision, before require_boot_lock flips.
#540 geometry cutover ordering: the FSBL compare growth and the tail check must fit the 38,912 B load span and land before the freeze. The current image is 28,704 B.
An RM0456 citation plus bench read-back on both boards (iota2 and pq1) before any *_MASK_PINNED flag flips.
Confirm on silicon that 0xFFFFFFFF un-sets a planted OEM lock at RDP-0; round 1 found RM0456 internally inconsistent on OEM2 write levels.
The production feature set cannot be built today (the S-2 fence blocks mode-production + optiga-trust-m), so the part C fix needs a cfg-level or source-invariant test rather than a production link.

merge.residual_after:
- An RDP or option-byte-load glitch at power-on still opens debug before any FSBL or secure-world instruction runs, so no check fires. Only SRAM_RST (#82) and the fact that secrets are PIN-gated in the SEs limit it.
- With halt rather than wipe, a stolen unit whose posture was weakened stays intact for repeated physical attempts, bounded by the SE PIN counters and E120.
- A single-fault attacker can still force one of the two tz-1 passes to read 'match' (accepted trade-off).
- Until the factory BOOT_LOCK ceremony lands, secure code can still move SECBOOTADD0 and SWAP_BANK at RDP-2.
- The FSBL code is not hidden or made non-executable until HDP1 (#39).
- OEM key absence is inferred from lock bits only. A factory that plants a key and a matching fake read-back is caught only by the user's own SWD read of NSSR.
- A compromised secure image can lie on the advisory fingerprint row regardless of the tail check.
- Nothing here detects BOR or WRP tampering on bench units, which carry no WRP.
merge.rationale: All five members describe the same gap, and it has two cheap real halves. The two predicates that decide whether invariant #10 holds are unpinned, and one of them is known wrong. One production verdict has no action. Everything else the members add is either already tracked, or is a port of Trezor's repair-and-erase that this project has explicitly rejected twice. Priority is P1, not P0: the unpinned predicates fail closed, so this is a ship blocker rather than a live hole, and nothing has shipped. Cost M is dominated by the silicon ceremony; the firmware parts are each S.

skeptic.reason:
The core survives: the two predicates that gate invariant #10 are unpinned, the OEM-lock mask is on the wrong bits, and one production verdict has no action. I confirmed these in code, the SVD and RM0456 Rev 7. Wipe and the on-device OEM key write were correctly dropped (Draft 1.2 C1 at fw-rollback-draft12-candidate-2026-07-21.md:66-72, first-boot-requirements.md R2.1, tz-1 decision at :397-407). All 24 tracked issues exist and are OPEN.

Several parts are over-valued or rest on a wrong reading of RM0456, though:

- **SECBOOTADD0 is frozen at RDP-2 regardless of BOOT_LOCK.** RM0456 Rev 7 §7.6.2 ("Option bytes cannot be programmed nor erased except the SWAP_BANK option bit") and the OPTWERR list ("to modify the option bytes, except the SWAP_BANK option bit, when RDP is set to level 2") say so. Threat (c), the residual "secure code can still move SECBOOTADD0 at RDP-2", and the post-lock reach of live defect 1 are therefore wrong. Only SWAP_BANK (and the DUALBANK rule) is at stake post-lock, and tz-1 already checks SWAP_BANK.
- **OEM keys cannot be written at RDP-2** (RM0456 §7.6.x: OEM1KEY modifiable at RDP 0/0.5/1, OEM2KEY at 0/0.5/1). WRP, OEM locks, BOOT_LOCK and BOR_LEV are all immutable post-lock. Part B's every-boot re-check can only detect a state Phase A already gated, i.e. a Phase A that was fault-skipped. It is an FI tripwire, not a new detector.
- **An OEM2-key holder regresses RDP under reset before any instruction runs** (RM0456: "it is not possible to execute instructions when the key is matching"). No post-lock firmware check stops the actual attack. The Phase-A gate and the user's SWD read are the only effective controls.
- **Every on-device check runs in flash the RDP-0 transit attacker can rewrite.** They stop only an attacker who alters option bytes but leaves flash genuine. The SWD checklist item in part E is the load-bearing control and should lead the package.
- **Part E's reset-cause gate is bypassed by the attack it targets.** A voltage glitch presents as BOR, which is classified Cold (secure/src/reset_cause.rs:182-184) and allowed.
- **The fw_update COMMIT tail check is moot today.** cmd_fw_commit refuses fail-closed (secure/src/nsc/cmd_fw_commit.rs:12-36,192), and erase_slot already erases the whole slot at BEGIN.

Feasibility is fine: no board change, FSBL growth of a few hundred bytes against 4,064 B of headroom in the 32 KiB region, and a tail compare of at most ~0.1 s. No conflict with a recorded decision remains after the drops. The tz-1 decision text itself already names "OPTR/WRP/SECWM", so widening the FSBL compare is inside it.
skeptic.corrections:
1. **Fix the RM0456 reading.** Delete "secure code can still move SECBOOTADD0 ... at RDP-2" from the threat and residual. At RDP-2 only SWAP_BANK remains writable. BOOT_LOCK's post-lock value is locking SWAP_BANK/DUALBANK; pre-lock it locks SECBOOTADD0. The comment in verify_ship_profile (shared/src/lockdown.rs, BOOT_LOCK block: "a clear BOOT_LOCK also leaves SECBOOTADD0 and SWAP_BANK mutable at RDP-2 (RM0456 §7.4.2)") carries the same stale claim and should be corrected in the pin commit.

2. **Re-scope part C.** The SECBOOTADD0 secure-world halt is P3 hygiene (FI / option-byte-load-glitch tripwire only).
   - Pre-lock it must not fire before Phase A. The check at main.rs:1280 runs before ui::init (:1620) and before first_boot (:1630), so a halt there is a blank-screen halt that hides the R5.1 E08xx code. Let Phase A own the pre-lock case and gate the new halt on RDP==L2, two-pass, with a visible code (#835).
   - Keep the #192 fix and the source-invariant "verdict whose only effect is secure_log!" test.

3. **Re-scope part B.**
   - FSBL leg: keep at P2, justified by the freeze asymmetry. Flipping *_MASK_PINNED does not make it deployable: bench units carry no WRP, BOOT_LOCK or raised BOR, and verify_ship_profile compares against FSBL_LAST_PAGE_FROZEN (page 4) while the linker still occupies pages 0..3 (#540). The FSBL needs an explicit production-profile cfg or a bench/ship split; otherwise every bench board halts.
   - Secure-world every-boot re-check: demote to optional/P3. The fields are immutable at RDP-2, and Phase A, which lives in the same updatable image, already gated them. Trezor's kernel re-check exists because Trezor repairs option bytes; that rationale does not port.

4. **Part A.**
   - Land the one-line 18/19 correction now, with a host test bound to the SVD values. It is independent of the silicon ceremony and removes a vacuous-pass trap. The current 26/27 coincide with OPTR nSWBOOT0/nBOOT0 (#46 body; secure/src/hw/dev_dfu.rs:42-43), which is likely where the guess came from.
   - The positive-detection test must provision an OEM2 key, not only OEM1. OEM2 is what governs the 2→1 regression; OEM1 governs 1→0.
   - Keys are 64-bit: write OEM1KEYR1/R2 and OEM2KEYR1/R2 (Trezor option_bytes.c:219-222).
   - RM0456 Rev 7 is consistent that both keys are modifiable at RDP-0 regardless of the lock bit, and that the lock bit is latched at option-byte load. The factory must OBL or power-cycle before reading NSSR.
   - The exact compare of nSWBOOT0/nBOOT0 has near-zero post-lock security value: RDP-2 disables system-memory boot, and with TZEN=1 the BOOT0 path leads only to ROM RSS (RM0456 Table 26; no SECBOOTADD1 exists on U5). Treat it as reliability.

5. **Part D.**
   - Drop or defer the COMMIT tail check to the FA-1/manifest-v6 path.
   - The claim "measure the whole slot window" overstates coverage. The inactive slot, the manifest pages, the page between the manifests and the slot, and the rest of secure bank 1 stay unmeasured; Phase A blank-checks only pages 123-127 (first_boot/mod.rs:201-205).
   - A tail payload is inert without a control-flow hijack, so this is P2/P3.
   - The check itself is feasible. The ui-px atlas sits at NS ORIGIN+0x1000, inside the declared length (nonsecure/memory-stm32u585-px.x:21), so it does not collide. Worst-case tail is under 976 KB of compare at HSI16, roughly 0.1 s against 2.9 s of verify; not blocking.

6. **Drop part E's reset-cause gate.**
   - BOR/glitch is classified Cold and allowed, so the gate misses its target.
   - A PINRSTF-only reset is classified Unknown (reset_cause.rs:187-190). A user who has just done the documented SWD connect-under-reset verification could be refused until a power cycle.
   - A hardware-mode IWDG during the indefinite confirm wait would loop.

7. **Promote the user SWD checklist and the #595 factory record to the head of the package** (P1, docs/tooling only). user-device-verification.md has no OEM/NSSR line; line 87 lists option bytes generically. Lead for the ceremony, untested: per RM0456 §7.6.2, at RDP-2 SWD stays alive under reset when an OEM2 key exists and is "definitively disabled" otherwise. That would be an external post-lock observable for a planted OEM2 key.
